# Branch

A `Branch` adds a collection of related records to a model. For a payment,
recent transactions can provide context about the account's usual activity.
Fields within each transaction stay together.

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    recent_transactions=rf.Branch(
        length=32,
        overflow="tail",
        days_ago=rf.Number,
        amount=rf.Number,
        merchant=rf.Category,
    ),
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

One labeled payment, with its earlier transactions ordered oldest to newest:

```yaml
amount: 42.75
merchant: grocery
recent_transactions:
  - days_ago: 3
    amount: 18.20
    merchant: grocery
  - days_ago: 1
    amount: 65.00
    merchant: fuel
disputed: false
```

`length=32` keeps at most 32 transactions. `overflow="tail"` keeps the most
recent ones when the application supplies this order. A
[preprocessor](../guides/preprocessors.qmd) owns sorting and calculating
`days_ago`.

## Binding and shape

The parent keyword supplies the collection name. With `query=None`,
`recent_transactions` reads the same-named child collection, and its leaves read
keys within each transaction. Use a [query](../core-concepts/querypaths.qmd) for
a different structural path and a preprocessor for sorting, filtering, or derived
values.

A child branch requires a list of objects, including when `length=1`. Only
the generated model root reads one object directly. Each child branch adds a
repeated axis. Its execution width follows the selected collections in each
batch; an explicit `length` caps retained items. Padding does not contribute to
attention or reduction, but it still has storage and processing costs.

Definitions are reusable: binding clones them without changing the original.
Use `fields={"length": rf.Number}` for generated schemas or child names that
collide with configuration. Use [Set](set.qmd) for membership alone and
[Vector](vector.qmd) for one numeric vector.

## Automatic Lengths And Limits

Omitting `length`, or setting `length=None`, retains every collection slot:

```python
history = rf.Branch(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
)
```

Each batch uses the largest retained collection length, including null object
slots. Widths can grow or shrink between batches; all-empty collections have
width zero. Nested widths are resolved after any parent limit has selected its
records. Leaves beneath the same branch share its geometry, independently of
values, masking, or which target is supplied. This changes execution geometry,
without updating the schema, growing parameters, or replacing the optimizer.

Set a positive integer `length` for a hard limit. Only bounded branches accept
`overflow="head"`, `"tail"`, or `"error"`; omission or `None` selects `"head"`
when a limit exists. `Branch(overflow="tail", ...)` without a finite length is
an error. The generated root always remains a singleton with `length=1` and
internal `overflow="error"`.

Bounded branches also pad only to the largest retained length in each batch,
up to their cap. [Prediction output](../guides/prediction-output.qmd#repeated-coordinates)
keeps a fixed-size Arrow axis for a finite limit and uses a variable-size list
for `length=None`.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Inference-time DoS/DDoS attack vector

With `length=None`, untrusted requests control nested collection sizes during
inference. Oversized collections can exhaust CPU/GPU memory or compute and deny
service to other users. Requests from multiple sources can amplify this into a
distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack.

Set finite branch lengths and enforce request-size limits before
[public serving](../guides/serving.qmd#bound-public-requests). A batch-size limit
alone does not bound nested collections. RelFlow logs one aggregate warning per
model generation for active unbounded branches; the warning enforces no limit.
No hidden cap is applied to `length=None`.
:::

Existing Python or YAML definitions that omit `length` now retain all items;
use `length=1` to retain the previous singleton limit. Existing checkpoints
with numeric lengths keep those explicit limits. Unbounded branches serialize
and restore with null length and overflow; batch widths are never saved as limits.

## Options

These are the direct `rf.Branch` defaults. A
[size preset](../core-concepts/model-tree.qmd#choose-a-size) such as
`Model.xs` fills omitted branch settings; explicit node settings take precedence.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | `None` | Named child mapping, combinable with keyword children; names must be unique. |
| `query` | `None` | Optional node-relative structural path. |
| `length` | `None` | Retain all items, or set a positive integer maximum per parent coordinate. |
| `overflow` | `None` | For finite lengths: keep first items (`"head"`, the bounded default), last items (`"tail"`), or raise (`"error"`). Unbounded branches keep `None`. Order comes from the processed source. |
| `attention` | `"mha"` | Encoder mode; see below. |
| `n_layers` | `1` | Positive sequence-encoder depth. |
| `n_heads` | `4` | Positive, even encoder head count and fallback for Attention reduction. Active attention requires heads to divide `d_model` with at least two dimensions per head. |
| `ffnx` | `8` | Positive integer feed-forward multiplier for this branch's encoders and learned reduction. See [model-tree configuration](../core-concepts/model-tree.qmd#configure-the-context). |
| `reduction` | `rf.Attention()` | What encoded memory reaches the parent. |
| `dropout` | `None` | Optional encoder dropout in `[0, 1)` and reduction fallback. |
| `mask` | `False` | [Masking policy](../core-concepts/dynamic-masking.qmd) applied atomically to active descendants. |
| `embed` | `False` | Export this branch's contextual embedding. |
| `description` | `None` | Human-readable notes. |

Branch settings are local. Model settings configure the generated singleton
root; they do not replace every child branch's defaults.

## Attention and reduction {#reduce-branch-memory}

An attention-enabled branch first mixes direct sibling leaves at each aligned
record coordinate, when there is more than one. Its `n_layers` sequence stack
then mixes child slots across the branch. Finally, reduction chooses the
representations routed to its parent.

| Encoder mode | Key/value heads |
| --- | --- |
| `"mha"` | One per query head. |
| `"gqa"` | One per pair of query heads. |
| `"mqa"` | One shared by every query head. |
| `None` | No coordinate or sequence attention; reduction still runs. |

Sharing key/value heads changes model capacity as well as cost.

| Reduction | Parent receives | Tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rf.Attention(n_outputs=1)` | A fixed number of learned summaries. | Bounded memory; outputs do not guarantee item identity. |
| `rf.Mean()` | One average of present encoded vectors. | Cheap; count, order, and individual values are not directly preserved. |
| `None` | Every encoded child slot with its presence state. | Keeps token correspondence available; increases parent sequence cost. |

`Attention` has `n_outputs=1`, `n_layers=1`, `n_heads=None`, `dropout=None`,
and `position=True`. Counts are positive. Omitted heads and dropout inherit
from the branch; explicit values override them. `position` controls rotary
position in the reducer only. `Mean` has no tuning options. These configurations
are frozen and share settings, not learned weights, when reused.

`attention=None` and `reduction=None` skip different operations. Use both for
pure pass-through. Turning off reducer position alone does not remove position
information from earlier encoder attention.

Choose reduction from the evidence the parent needs. A mean is not a raw-field
sum, and more learned summaries do not perform a join. Capacity must survive
later reductions too. `model.schema.branch_outputs` reports each branch's
static routed width, or `None` when pass-through width depends on the batch.

The [nested cardinality proof](../proofs/structure/attention-preserves-nested-cardinality.html)
tests whether session summaries preserve enough information for their parent.
The [Mean control](../proofs/structure/mean-erases-cardinality.html) isolates what
is lost when identical repeated values become one normalized summary.

## Masks and output

A branch mask makes one decision per retained branch coordinate and applies it
to the whole descendant subtree. A reconstructing policy creates leaf
objectives; the branch has no typed decoder of its own. Structural skipping
omits selected inputs from tensorization and attention.

`embed=True` exports branch context at its address. See
[Embeddings](../core-concepts/embeddings.qmd) for output roles and
[Model tree](../core-concepts/model-tree.qmd) for the route through nested contexts.
